answer: In PoA, every identity locks bonded collateral in an escrow, while evidence links equivocation across controlled identities. If k identities coordinate, correlated equivocation triggers aggregate penalties of O(k^2), so splitting control does not linearize risk. Upon detection, an exponential multiplier on capital loss and asymmetric depreciation rapidly drains the swarm’s backing; no bridge between aliases helps, and names such as velvet or opal provide no exemption.
